text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A deputy of the Latvian parliament, Ivars Janis Kezbers, died in Strasbourg.

- Interpol officials arrested Latvian citizen Boris Karpichkov on April 21 at Sheremetyevo airport in Moscow. He is accused of embezzeling G-24 loans. He is due to be extradited to Latvian authorities shortly.
- Delegations from Latvia, Estonia and Russia agreed on the location of the crossing point of the three countries' state borders.

- Representatives of the three major ruling factions met with president Guntis Ulmanis to discuss the naturalisation of ethnic Poles ahead of his presidential visit to Warsaw. Fatherland & Freedom is still opposed to the proposal.
- President Kwasniewski of Poland told Latvian journalists that his country supports Latvia's integration with the EU and NATO.

- The contract on leasing the Riga railway terminal to the Norwegian group Varner Hakon Invest is due to be signed shortly after being approved by the ministry of transportation. Under the contract, the group is to invest $6 million to reconstruct the building.
-The captain of a Panamanian ship, Astra, was fined 150 lats for not raising the Latvian flag while approaching the harbour of Riga.

- Two-year T-bills debuted with an annual yield of 9.5 percent. The government offered to the commercial banks bills worth 17.5 million lats. Finance minister Roberts Zile told the press the auction represents another step in the development of Latvia's financial market raises the prestige of the government's bonds.
